You're right that it's genuinely hard - there is no known way to fully prevent prompt injection when you feed untrusted text to an LLM. But you can reduce the risk a lot with cheap, layered defenses: delimit the untrusted text, tell the model it is data not instructions, and strip hidden content before it reaches the prompt.

I have the full picture. The reader faithfully extracts whatever text is on the page - including hidden text - and that flows straight into the LLM prompts with zero sanitization. An advertiser could embed 'Ignore previous instructions' and it would be treated as page content by the summariser.
